preamble: Raising of the near-open front vowel [æ] to open-mid [ɛ] is documented as the first step of the New Zealand English short front vowel shift, in which TRAP rose into the space formerly occupied by DRESS, and as a regional realization of TRAP in South African English.

examples.note: In the short front vowel chain shift TRAP rose from near-open [æ] to open-mid [ɛ], while DRESS rose toward [e] and KIT centralized to [ə]; Cultivated NZE retains [æ].
TRAP ranges from [æ] to [ɛ] in General and Cultivated South African English and can be as close as [ɛ̝] in Broad SAE.
